(1) the growth rates of magnetorotatonal instability in radiation-dominated accretion disks are consistent with the predictions of linear theory, (2) the turbulent fluctuations produced by this instability are much larger than in gas pressure-dominated disks, and (3) the turbulent fluctuations are damped by radiation diffusion.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a numerical code for the simulation of the dynamics of the accretion disk around a black hole.
the development of a theory of the dynamics of the interstellar medium, which is based upon the fundamental laws of physics.
the study of the dynamics of accretion flows around compact objects.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the magnetorotational-instability is a viable mechanism for angular-momentum transport in the inner regions of disks surrounding black holes, where radiation dominates gas pressure.
the MRI in radiation-dominated disks is qualitatively similar to the MRI in gas pressure-dominated disks, but the MRI is more vigorous and the resulting turbulent fluctuations are larger.
radiation pressure does not alter the basic character of the MRI, but the MRI is altered by radiation pressure in a number of important ways.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
radiation effects can significantly modify the structure and dynamics of radiation pressure-dominated accretion disks.
the magnetorotational turbulence is a robust mechanism for angular momentum transport, and the radiation pressure can significantly modify the disk structure and the turbulence.
the growth rates of the MRI are consistent with the predictions of linear analysis, and that radiation pressure can have a dramatic effect on the saturation of the instability.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the MRI is not suppressed in radiation-dominated disks, but that its nonlinear evolution is significantly different from that of gas pressure-dominated disks.

the MRI can be important in the inner regions of radiation-dominated accretion disks, where the magnetic field is dynamically important and the instability can be driven by the vertical component of magnetic field.
the magnetorotational turbulence that is so effective at transporting angular momentum in gas pressure-dominated disks also transports energy in radiation pressure-dominated disks.
